# Manuscript tables and numbers (generated; do not edit by hand)

Generated by `revision_pipeline/paper_results.py` from committed outputs only. Every exact value is in `results/paper_numbers.json`; the tables below round for printing. Families are evaluated at matched configurations: each family's own structural best configuration and threshold percentile, for every criterion. The production model is kNN with n_neighbors = 21, cosine distance, distance weighting, thresholds at P50 (`KNeighborsClassifier` below).

## 6. Model selection (Section 2.3.5, Table 8)

Source: `results/selection/selection_table.csv`; `results/winner_and_constants.json`; `results/selection/baselines.csv`.

Rule (`select_model.rule_balanced_maximin`): among the eligible families that pass the adequacy floor (PenalizedObj >= 0.5), each criterion is min-max normalized across those families; the score is the smallest of the three normalized values; the highest score wins (ties by PenalizedObj). Criteria, all at the family's structural best configuration and percentile: PenalizedObj (Eq. 19), CV macro AUC (mean of 5 repeats), held-out within-one-level accuracy over accepted verbs (full production pipeline, mean of outer seeds 13 to 17).

| GaussianNB | var_smoothing=1e-09, P40 | 0.721 | 0.711 | 0.706 | 0.000 | 0.810 | 0.318 | 0.000 | obj |
| Legacy kNN (reference, not eligible) | unweighted, K=15/th=0.28/c=6 | 1.004 | n/a | n/a |  |  |  | n/a |  |
| QDA | reg_param=0.05, P60 | 0.166 | 0.619 | 0.554 |  |  |  | below floor |  |
| LDA | shrinkage=auto, P60 | 0.011 | 0.628 | 0.560 |  |  |  | below floor |  |

Selected: **KNeighborsClassifier** (n_neighbors=21, P50), score 0.713; runner-up CalibratedSVC 0.552; margin 0.161. The production model's score is limited by its normalized PenalizedObj (n_obj = 0.713).

Trivial reference for the held-out criterion: predicting the majority level (Ap) for every verb gives within-one 0.669 [0.622, 0.717] (all verbs accepted); prevalence-proportional random levels give 0.621. The production model reaches 0.742 over the verbs it accepts and 0.692 over all held-out verbs (a rejected verb counts as a miss).

For comparison (Section 3.1), the first-revision two-stage form of the rule (stage-one maximin of PenalizedObj and CV AUC, shortlist, then maximin with held-out seed 13 re-normalized inside the shortlist), applied to the same matched inputs, selects **CalibratedSVC** with 0.170. Shortlist: CalibratedSVC, LogisticRegression, NearestCentroid, KNeighborsClassifier. The production model scores 0.000 there because, re-normalized inside the shortlist, its CV AUC (0.7135) is the lowest, 0.0023 below the next (NearestCentroid, 0.7158). Section 9 below reports how this depends on the inputs.

Source: `results/selection/matched_supervised.csv`; `results/selection/mcnemar_vs_production.csv`.

Differences are other family minus kNN-21 P50. Bootstrap: 95% percentile bootstrap, 10000 resamples of the 381 verbs with replacement, numpy default_rng(13), identical resamples for every configuration and repeat (paired); avg5 = statistic averaged over the 5 repeats inside each resample. Exact McNemar tests on the held-out decision 'primary accepted and within one level' (all held-out verbs); one test per outer seed, not corrected for multiplicity. The pooled count over the 5 seeds reuses the same verbs and is descriptive only.

Families whose CV AUC and held-out within-one intervals both include zero: 3 of 8. A single-seed p below 0.05 is not evidence that kNN-21 is better: it is uncorrected, seed 13 is kNN-21's most favourable repeat, and the other seeds do not repeat it.

Legacy kNN, when admitted, wins the rule in use; it is excluded on eligibility grounds (one global vote cutoff, no per-level calibrated scores, not exportable by retrain.py), not on performance. Its evaluation-only numbers: CV macro AUC 0.705, held-out within-one 0.739 (accepted) and 0.688 (all verbs). The adequacy floor is absolute while the SCS scale moves with the weights, so in some joint draws fewer families pass it.
